title: Saturn's moon Enceladus sprays ice into space
body: NASA's Cassini spacecraft photographed plumes of icy material rising from the south polar region of Enceladus in 2005. The jets emerge near long fractures in the moon's crust known as tiger stripes.
takeaway: A passing spacecraft can sample what a moon ejects without landing on it.
source: NASA Cassini, Spray Above Enceladus III (2006)
visual: thin jets of ice rising above the curved edge of Saturn's moon Enceladus
